'''Aedo Hashihime Shrine''' (饗土橋姫神社) is an auxiliary shrine (shokansha) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} (Naikū) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It enshrines the {{ill|Guardian deities|ja|守護神|qid=Q131278957|lt=Guardian deity}} of the {{ill|Uji Bridge (Ise City)|ja|宇治橋|qid=Q23997081|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise)}}, located directly opposite the bridge.<ref name="ic6">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.116</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.54</ref>
As the shrine's {{ill|Shinto architecture|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/main hall (Shinto)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/main hall (Shinto)|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=神社建築|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} is rebuilt prior to the reconstruction of the Uji Bridge, it becomes the first {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} among the 125 shrines under the jurisdiction of Ise Grand Shrine to be rebuilt during the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengu}}.<ref name="um8">Ise Bunka-sha (2009): p.58</ref>
== Overview ==
Located about 200 [[:en:Meters|m]] from the {{ill|Uji Bridge (Ise City)|ja|宇治橋|qid=Q23997081|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise)}}, the entrance to the sacred precincts of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine) in {{ill|Uji|ja|宇治今在家町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji-Imazaike-chō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji-Imazaike-chō|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=宇治 (伊勢市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11449448}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ar|إيسه|azb|ایسه، میه|bcl|Ise, Mie|be|Ісэ (горад)|ca|Ise (ciutat japonesa)|ce|Исе (гӀала)|ckb|ئیسێ|cs|Ise (Mie)|de|Ise (Mie)|eo|Ise (urbo)|es|Ise (Mie)|et|Ise (Jaapan)|eu|Ise (Mie)|fa|ایسه، میه|fi|Ise (kaupunki)|fr|Ise (Mie)|gl|Ise|hr|Ise|hy|Իսե (քաղաք)|id|Ise, Mie|it|Ise (Giappone)|ja|伊勢市|ka|ისე|ko|이세시|lt|Isė (Japonija)|mg|Ise|mzn|ایسه، میه|nl|Ise (Mie)|no|Ise (Mie)|pl|Ise (Japonia)|pt|Ise (Japão)|ro|Ise, Japonia|ru|Исе (город)|sh|Ise|simple|Ise, Mie|sr|Исе|sv|Ise, Japan|szl|Ise (Japůńijo)|tg|Исе|tl|Ise, Mie|tr|Ise (şehir)|tt|Исе (шәһәр)|uk|Ісе (Міє)|ur|ایسے، میہ|uz|Ise (Mie)|vi|Ise, Mie|war|Ise, Mie|zh|伊勢市|zh_classical|伊勢市|zh_min_nan|Ise-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}<ref name="ic1">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p.111</ref>. Approximately 20 m ahead of {{ill|Aedo Hashihime Shrine|ja|饗土橋姫神社}}, you’ll find the {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社}}, {{ill|Nīkawa Shrine|ja|新川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkawa Shrine (Ise)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkawa Shrine (Ise)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11502105}}, and {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|石井神社|lt=Ishii Shrine (Ise)}}, all subordinate shrines (摂末社) of the Inner Shrine. Another 50 m further are {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|大水神社}}, {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|大水神社|lt=Kawai Shrine}}, and {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|大水神社|lt=Kumabuchi Shrine}}, making a total of seven shrines clustered together<ref>Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): pp.111, 116</ref>. Additionally, the predecessor to the {{ill|Jingū Library|ja|神宮文庫}}, the former {{ill|Jingū Library|ja|林崎文庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashizaki Library|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashizaki Library|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=神宮文庫|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11589490}}, is located nearby<ref>Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p.117</ref>. Adjacent to the shrine, further along the path to the left, is the {{ill|Gōkaku Shrine|ja|合格神社|qid=DELETED_QID}}, dedicated to {{ill|Yukio Ozaki|en|Yukio Ozaki|qid=Q1152666|lt=Ozaki Yukio}}.
The name "Aedo" (饗土) refers to land designated for rituals to appease or prevent the entry of evil spirits and deities associated with plagues and disasters through offerings and ceremonies<ref name="um8"/>. The shrine grounds were relocated during the construction of {{ill|Miyuki Road|ja|御幸道路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyuki Road|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyuki Road|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22222736}}<ref>Ise City, ed. (2012): Vol.4, p.551</ref>. Since the reconstruction in {{ill|1969|en|1969|qid=Q2485|lt=1969}} (Shōwa 44), the shrine has not been moved<ref name="um63">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2009): p.63</ref>.
While the current shrine architecture follows the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, this was adopted during the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}. Prior to that, the shrine was built in the {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|en|Kasuga-zukuri|qid=Q3193781|lt=Kasuga-zukuri}} style<ref>Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2009): p.59</ref>. {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社}} Ranks 14th among the 27 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp.9–10</ref>.
=== deity ===
The enshrined deity is the guardian deity of Uji Bridge (宇治橋鎮守神, Ujibashi no Mamori no Kami)<ref name="ic6"/> <ref name="gk"/>. It is venerated as the protective deity of Uji Bridge<ref name="ic6"/> <ref name="gk"/>.
*{{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社|lt=Niikawa Shrine}}
*{{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社|lt=Iwai Shrine}}
*{{ill|Otsuchi Mioya Shrine|ja|大土御祖神社|lt=Uji-no-Nuki Shrine}}
== History ==
The origin of the {{ill|Uji Bridge (Ise City)|ja|宇治橋|qid=Q23997081|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise)}} remains unknown,<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2009): p. 49</ref> and likewise, the establishment date of the {{ill|Aedo Hashihime Shrine|ja|饗土橋姫神社}}, which guards Uji Bridge, is also unclear.<ref>{{Cite web|language=ja|url=http://www.sengu.info/news/005-000150.html|title=宇治橋修造起工式おこなわれる|publisher=Ise Jingū Shikinen Sengū PR Office|date=2008-07-31|accessdate=2013-10-27|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1027-2243-59/www.sengu.info/news/005-000150.html|archivedate=2013-10-27}}</ref> However, it is believed to have existed prior to the reconstruction of Uji Bridge in {{ill|Civilization|en|Civilization|qid=Q8432|lt=Bunmei}} 9 (1477), as records indicate the shrine was rebuilt at that time.<ref name="um3">Ise Bunka-sha (2009): p. 53</ref> According to issue 211 of ''Mizugaki,'' published by the {{ill|Jingū Administration Office|ja|神宮司庁}}, and based on "Regarding Aedo Hashihime Shrine" by Jingū priest Satoru Otowa, the large bridge resembling the current form is said to have been donated and visited by {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshinori|en|Ashikaga Yoshinori|qid=Q239170|lt=Ashikaga Yoshinori}} in {{ill|Eikyō|en|Eikyō|qid=Q1193059|lt=Eikyō}} 6 (1435) as recorded in the ''Kawasaki Clan Chronicle.''
{{ill|Arakida Moriyoshi|ja|荒木田守良|qid=DELETED_QID}} explains in ''Jingū Tenryaku'' that the shrine was established in {{ill|Kanshō|en|Kanshō|qid=Q1143928|lt=Kanshō}} 7 (1467), in conjunction with Ashikaga Yoshinori's pilgrimage, modeled after the {{ill|Hashihime Shrine|ja|橋姫神社|lt=Hashihime Shrine (Kyoto)}} on the Uji Bridge in Kyoto, dedicated to {{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津姫}}. Unlike Kyoto's Uji, where shrines are placed directly on the bridge, Aedo Hashihime Shrine was never associated with tales of curses, vengeful spirits, or yokai folklore. The original location was near the famous photo spot just in front of Uji Bridge, around the torii gate and pine grove area, which previously featured two cherry trees instead of pines.
During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the shrine was managed by the self-governing body of Uji known as the "Uji Kaigosho."<ref name="st3">Sakurai (1991): p. 273</ref> In {{ill|Bunsei|en|Bunsei|qid=Q1327119|lt=Bunsei}} 13 (1830), the shrine burned down along with Uji Bridge.<ref name="um63"/> In June of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 5 (July 1872), the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|en|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|qid=Q4294653|lt=Ministry of Religion}} removed shrines not listed in the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'' or the ''Enryaku Gishikichō'' from Jingū's jurisdiction, transferring them to the administration of {{ill|Watarai Prefecture|ja|度会県|zh|度會縣|fr|Préfecture de Watarai|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Prefecture|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Prefecture|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Prefecture|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Prefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486130}} and later Mie Prefecture. As a result, Aedo Hashihime Shrine was separated from Jingū’s management.<ref>Sakurai (1991): pp. 266, 272–273</ref> Uji Bridge and the torii in front of it were also transferred to Watarai Prefecture simultaneously.<ref name="um3"/>

Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 22 (1889), as part of the 56th {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengū}}, Uji Bridge was reconstructed with national funds. Since Aedo Hashihime Shrine's prefectural status posed issues for the bridge’s ceremonial usage, the shrine was reinstated under the Inner Shrine’s jurisdiction.<ref name="st3"/> Upon its return to Jingū, the shrine retained its July 21 festival to respect local traditions.<ref name="st3"/>
The shrine was originally located immediately next to Uji Bridge. However, due to the construction of a national road (Miyuki Road) in December {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 40 (1907), the shrine site overlapped with the new road. Consequently, in March {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 42 (1909), a new site was established between {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|大水神社}} and {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社}}, and the shrine was relocated.<ref name="sk">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 244</ref> Since the shrine’s reconstruction in {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 44 (1969), its location has remained unchanged.<ref name="um63"/>

== Rites ==
A religious ceremony is held on the occasion of the "Uji Bridge Crossing Ceremony" <ref name="ic6"/><ref name="gk"/>. A religious ceremony is also offered at the "Uji Bridge Repair Groundbreaking Ceremony" held when the new Uji Bridge is constructed <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book| url=http://ise.jr-central.co.jp/ujibashi/1st/report.html |title=Uji Bridge|Let's go. Ise-Shima| publisher=[[Tokai Railway Company]]|date= 2008th year July 26th |accessdate=2013-11-02 |archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1102-1709-53/ise.jr-central.co.jp/ujibashi/1st/report.html |archivedate=2013-11-02}}</ref>.
